prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of proposals and costings

Funding and tax
- Redirect around £5bn per year from lower-priority programmes: abolish a central industry department and subsidies; cancel ID cards; repurpose the Child Trust Fund to cut class sizes.
- Introduce a 50% income tax rate on earnings over £100,000 to fund approximately £4.9bn annually for: abolishing student tuition/top-up fees, free personal care, and lower local taxes.
- Replace Council Tax with a Local Income Tax based on ability to pay; typical households save about £450 per year.

Health and care
- Free personal care for elderly and disabled people.
- Faster diagnosis using the quickest practical route; expand scans/tests in primary care; extend evening/weekend capacity; publish diagnostic waits.
- Free eye and dental check-ups; broaden prescription charge exemptions for long-term conditions.
- Recruit more clinicians; reduce central targets; strengthen local accountability.
- Reform NHS dentistry; personal care plans; more palliative care and hospice support; modern mental health legislation; end age discrimination.
- Public health: school meal nutrition standards, restrict unhealthy food ads in children’s TV, ban smoking in enclosed public places.

Education and skills
- Abolish tuition and top-up fees; restore grants for students on lower incomes.
- Cut infant classes to average 20 and junior to 25 by funding 21,000 teachers; extend school hours 8am–6pm; complete 3,500 Children’s Centres by 2010.
- Ensure core subjects taught by qualified specialists; reduce high-stakes testing at 7 and 11 to sample-based assessment; strengthen discipline and SEND support.
- Create a unified diploma blending academic/vocational routes; close school–college funding gaps; modernise college facilities.
- Maintain statutory free school transport distances; expand safe routes to school.

Crime, justice, and borders
- Fund 10,000 additional police by cancelling ID cards; streamline paperwork and upgrade technology; 20,000 extra community support officers.
- Focus enforcement on traffickers and acquisitive crime linked to drug use; community payback for non-violent offenders; tougher licensing enforcement and late-night policing contributions.
- Prison: full working day, prioritise education/skills for rehabilitation.
- Create a UK Border Force; protect jury trial; allow intercept evidence in court; replace control orders with judge-led, time-limited measures subject to high proof.
- Asylum: new independent decision agency; allow asylum seekers to work; develop EU-wide standards.
- Single Equality Act; hate-crime units; equal pension treatment for civil partners.

Economy and business
- Independent audit of budget figures; strengthen statistics independence; curb irresponsible lending practices.
- Raise the stamp duty threshold to £150,000.
- Cut red tape: mandatory costed impact assessments, sunset clauses, single multi-purpose inspections.
- Small business rate relief up to £1,500; move to site-value rating; duty to trade fairly; bolster tourism with an English board.

Pensions, benefits, and families
- From age 75: raise basic pensions (linked to earnings) to at least £109.45 single and £167.05 couple; introduce a residency-based citizen’s pension at 75; Local Income Tax benefits for pensioners.
- First-child maternity pay at the minimum wage for six months (£170/week).
- Replace the Child Support Agency with HMRC-based assessments and a specialist tribunal.
- £200 Winter Fuel Payment for severely disabled working-age people; implement free personal care; improve compensation for failed workplace pensions; consult on public sector pension changes.
- Simplify benefits/tax credits; strengthen anti-fraud/error.

Housing, communities, and services
- Release public land for 100,000 affordable homes; incentivise brownfield/retrofit via VAT reform; require permission to convert homes to holiday use in pressured areas.
- Protect Post Office network; maintain universal postal pricing.
- Consolidate inspectorates; devolve powers to local government; streamline regional bodies; fairer intra-UK funding formula.

International, defence, and development
- Iraq: support transition, strengthen Iraqi forces and services, include Sunni leaders, aim to withdraw troops with UN mandate expiry.
- Work through UN/EU; reform international institutions; support the EU constitution subject to a referendum.
- Defence: avoid overextension; open procurement; reallocate from lower-priority programmes (e.g., later Eurofighter tranches) to personnel welfare and equipment; retain minimum nuclear deterrent pending multilateral reductions; strengthen arms export scrutiny.
- Development: raise aid to 0.5% GNI by 2007/08 and 0.7% by 2011; end trade barriers and agricultural dumping; promote responsible investment.

Rural affairs
- Food supply chain fairness via a legal duty to trade fairly and a Food Trade Inspector.
- Accelerate CAP reform toward public goods; support family farms and new entrants.
- Marine Act for spatial planning, conservation zones, and fisheries protection.
- Animal Protection Commission and comprehensive Animal Welfare Act; cautious approach to GM crops, support GM-free zones and organic farming.

Transport
- Rationalise rail franchising with longer contracts for investment; restore deferred upgrades; improve station safety.
- Reform VED to zero for the least-polluting cars and higher for the most polluting; encourage urban congestion charging tied to upfront public transport investment.
- Long-term shift to national road pricing by congestion/location/pollution, replacing fuel duty and VED.
- Free off-peak local bus travel for pensioners and disabled people; free rail discount cards for pensioners, disabled people, families, and young people.
- Limit major new roads; invest in public transport, cycling, and freight interchanges; aviation: per-aircraft charging, emissions trading, oppose new/expanded SE airports; protect lifeline routes.

Environmental measures
- Carbon Tax replacing the Climate Change Levy; incentives for efficient homes and low-emission vehicles.
- At least 20% electricity from renewables by 2020; do not replace ageing nuclear plants; support alternative fuels.
- REACH chemical safety; zero-waste goal with 60% household recycling within seven years; stronger building regulations; Environmental Responsibility Act; green public procurement.
- Lead global climate negotiations toward contraction and convergence; target aid to renewables, water, sustainable agriculture; combat environmental crime and protect biodiversity.
